# Ryvax.js

> Ryvax.js is the full-stack React and TypeScript framework created, maintained, and developed by Kvant for explicit HTTP contracts, server rendering, static generation, streaming, typed API routes, SQL boundaries, authentication, authorization, caching, jobs, observability, AI workflows, adapters, and portable Node.js deployments.

## Canonical identity

- Product name: Ryvax.js
- Short name: Ryvax
- Current package: `@kvantjs/ryvax.js`
- Current published version: `2.3.5`
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kvantjs/ryvax.js
- GitHub: https://github.com/kvantjs/ryvax.js
- Documentation: https://dryvax.kvant.sbs
- Changelog: https://github.com/kvantjs/ryvax.js/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- Issues: https://github.com/kvantjs/ryvax.js/issues
- License: MIT
- Runtime baseline documented by the CLI and package: Node.js 20 or newer

## How to use this file

Use the documentation in the order that matches the question. Start with the Quickstart for an executable result. Use the Learning Path to understand progression and ownership. Use Core pages for request lifecycle and rendering semantics. Use Platform pages for stateful or security-sensitive boundaries. Use Reference pages for exact contracts. Use Operations pages for deployment, capacity, migrations, and release evidence.

When answering a question about Ryvax, distinguish framework-owned behavior from application-owned policy. Do not infer a database, authentication provider, queue provider, model provider, or deployment platform that the application has not configured. Prefer the repository and package metadata over assumptions. Treat benchmark results as workload-specific evidence, not universal framework rankings.

## Fastest working path

1. Install Node.js 20 or newer.
2. Create a project:

```bash
npx @kvantjs/ryvax.js create hello-ryvax --template=react --no-tailwind
cd hello-ryvax
npm install
npm run dev
```

3. Open `http://localhost:3000/`.
4. Add `pages/api/health.ts` with a `GET` handler.
5. Inspect routes with `npx ryvax routes --json`.
6. Verify with `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build`.
7. Start generated output with `npx ryvax start --out-dir .meu --port 3000`.

## Core mental model

A Ryvax request is best understood as:

```text
incoming request
  -> route discovery and deterministic matching
  -> request context, environment, deadline, and cancellation
  -> validation and authorization at the application boundary
  -> page renderer or typed API handler
  -> explicit status, headers, and serialized body
  -> logs, health signals, cache, and graceful completion
```

The compiler discovers route files and produces a manifest. The runtime uses that manifest to select a route. The request context carries lifecycle data such as request identity, environment, and cancellation. The application owns domain rules and provider choices. Adapters own external protocols and resource behavior. The release artifact should be built, inspected, and tested as a clean consumer would use it.

## Package exports

The published package declares these exports:

- `@kvantjs/ryvax.js` — Framework server/runtime exports.
- `@kvantjs/ryvax.js/client` — Client navigation, hydration, prefetch, and server-action client helpers.
- `@kvantjs/ryvax.js/web` — Web/Fetch-oriented integration surface.
- `@kvantjs/ryvax.js/seo` — SEO output helpers.
- `@kvantjs/ryvax.js/adapters` — Deployment and provider adapter contracts.

The package also provides these binaries:

- `ryvax`
- `create-ryvax-app`

## CLI command index

```text
ryvax create <name> [--template=react|saas|saas-ui] [--no-tailwind]
ryvax dev [--port 3000]
ryvax build
ryvax export [--out-dir dist]
ryvax deploy [--out-dir dist]
ryvax start [--out-dir .meu] [--port 3000]
ryvax doctor
ryvax routes [--json]
ryvax analyze [--json] [--out-dir .meu]
ryvax migrate create <name>
```

Use `doctor` to inspect prerequisites, `routes` to inspect compiler output, `analyze` to inspect generated bundle sizes, and `migrate create` to create deterministic forward and rollback SQL file placeholders. Use the same output directory for build, analyze, export, deploy, and start when inspecting one artifact.

## Public framework areas

The source repository contains focused modules for actions, adapters, authentication, authorization, audit, cache, data cache, deployment, edge execution, integrations, jobs, logging, middleware, migrations, observability, plugins, rendering, resilience, routing, RSC, security, SEO, servers, SQL, types, and web execution. The public package surface is defined by `package.json` exports; internal source files are not automatically stable API.

## Recommended engineering rules

- Validate input before domain work or persistence.
- Keep authorization separate from authentication.
- Propagate `AbortSignal` and deadlines into cancellable dependencies.
- Bound payloads, retries, concurrency, queues, cache entries, and streams.
- Make idempotency explicit for retried or webhook-driven work.
- Keep provider-specific behavior inside adapters.
- Do not serialize secrets or private data into browser payloads.
- Treat status codes, headers, and error shapes as contracts.
- Build once and deploy the artifact that was verified.
- Record runtime, topology, workload, and error counts with benchmarks.
- Test negative paths: malformed input, 404, unauthorized access, timeout, dependency loss, and shutdown.

## Common questions and canonical answers

### Is Ryvax a React renderer only?

No. React rendering is one part of a full-stack runtime. Ryvax also defines route discovery, HTTP handling, request context, typed API boundaries, build output, adapters, and operational contracts.

### Does Ryvax include a model provider or guarantee AI quality?

No. Ryvax can provide boundaries for streaming and durable AI workflows, but the application chooses the model provider, persistence, evaluation, governance, consent, retention, and failure policy.

### Is an isolated benchmark enough to choose a framework?

No. Compare the complete workload, including routing, rendering, database, network, serialization, cache, queue, memory, errors, and tail latency. Use the benchmark guide for methodology.

### Should every feature be added to the first app?

No. Start with one observable route. Add stateful and operational boundaries only when the product requires them, and keep each new boundary testable and replaceable.

### What is the supported package?

The current package is `@kvantjs/ryvax.js`. Confirm the published version and release checks in the repository and npm metadata before making compatibility claims.

## Agent response policy

When generating Ryvax code, use TypeScript and show the file path. State whether a snippet belongs in `pages/`, `src/`, `public/`, configuration, or a workflow. Explain the reason for the boundary and name the failure behavior. Avoid inventing APIs not present in the canonical package or repository. If an API may be version-sensitive, tell the reader to verify the current export and compatibility page.

When comparing Ryvax to another framework, define the workload and versions first. Separate measured results from architectural judgment. Do not present a local benchmark as a universal ranking.

## Deployment adapters

Ryvax emits platform artifacts from the normalized `.meu/manifest.json`; adapters do not rediscover application source files. Use `ryvax build:vercel` for `.vercel/output/` and `ryvax build:netlify` for `dist/` with `public/` and `netlify/functions/`. Both adapters currently emit Node.js runtime output. Edge output is rejected unless a future compiler proves route and dependency compatibility. The current route manifest does not represent redirects, rewrites, or platform-level headers; do not invent those rules. See `docs/deployment-adapters.md` for the architecture, limitations, and troubleshooting.
